content:
lina_support: Hey team — customer (acme-inc) reporting 401 invalid_api_key when calling /v1/generate. They rotated keys yesterday and now see "HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized". They pasted a sanitized curl and response but obviously not the raw key.

omar_sre: Can you paste the exact curl they used and the full JSON error (redact the key)? Also the correlation id if present.

lina_support: Here are sanitized details from the customer:

`````
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live_***REDACTED***\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","input":"hello"}'
`````

Response:

`````
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  \"error\": {
    \"type\":\"invalid_api_key\",
    \"message\":\"API key is invalid or expired\",
    \"hint\":\"check key expiry or missing Bearer\"
  }
}
`````

Correlation: corr_20260315_9a7b
Time: 2026-03-15T14:22:10Z

priya_engineer: Two quick checks: (1) confirm there are no leading/trailing whitespace characters when the key is pasted; (2) check the key scope/permissions — did they accidentally create a management-only token or revoke inference scopes? Also, ask whether they tried the same key from a different machine.

lina_support: Asked the customer to run `GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/me` with the same header (redacted). They got 403 on that call. Customer mentioned they manage keys via SSO and recently rotated keys in the console.

omar_sre: 403 from /keys/me suggests the token used may not be an API key for that endpoint (could be an OAuth access token or a partially copied key). Confirm they aren't mixing OAuth bearer tokens and sk- API keys. Also check the Authorization header exact prefix is `Bearer sk-`.

lina_support: Customer confirmed header starts with `Bearer sk-`. They pasted the first 8 characters shown as `sk-live`.

priya_engineer: I'm pulling gateway logs for corr_20260315_9a7b now.

deploy-bot: [log snippet] 2026-03-15T14:22:10Z gateway request_id=corr_20260315_9a7b src=52.34.12.77 path=/v1/generate auth_type=api_key auth_id=sk_live_abc123 status=401 reason=invalid_api_key

omar_sre: auth_id looks redacted to sk_live_abc123 in logs (normal). Can the customer run a low-level check to verify hidden chars? Ask them to run: `echo -n \"<their_key_here>\" | od -An -t x1` to reveal non-printable bytes (e.g., 0a).

lina_support: Customer ran the od command and returned a trailing 0a byte after the key (newline). They had copied from a note that included a newline.

priya_engineer: Bingo. A trailing newline or other invisible char will change the HMAC/signature we check and the key will not match — gateway treats it as invalid. Recommend they strip whitespace, e.g. `KEY=$(cat keyfile | tr -d '\\n')` or `echo -n`. Also advise using the console copy button or storing keys in a secure secret manager.

lina_support: Sent fix steps to customer and asked them to retry. They re-ran the curl with a cleaned key and now see 200 OK and a successful response body. They confirmed correlation id corr_20260315_9a7b is no longer returning 401 for their new requests.

omar_sre: Adding action item: we should harden console copy behavior — trim trailing whitespace when copying and surface a small tooltip about non-printable chars. Filing internal ticket INF-4921.

priya_engineer: Also adding a short troubleshooting note to docs: common reasons for 401 invalid_api_key = expired key, wrong prefix (missing sk-), newline/whitespace in header, key revoked, mixing OAuth vs API key.

lina_support: Marking this resolved on the customer's side. Will follow up in 24h to ensure no regressions. :thumbsup:

omar_sre: Thanks team. Closing thread.
